newsitem.title: UK: Illness forces Britain to drop war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: Illness forces Britain to drop war crimes trial.

text.p: Britain abandoned its first warcrimes trial on Friday after a court ruled that the defendant, 86-year-old Szymon Serafinowicz, was not mentally fit to be tried.
Doctors had told Britain's Central Criminal Court that Serafinowicz, a postwar refugee from Byelorussia, was suffering from dementia, probably caused by Alzheimer's disease.
"The result of this (decision) is that all proceedings in this case are stayed," said prosecuting lawyer Sir Derek Spencer.
Serafinowicz had faced three charges of killing Jews in Byelorussia during the winter of 1941-42, when the former Soviet republic was under Nazi occupation. He had denied the charges.
He was a commander in a police force set up by the Nazis after they invaded Byelorussia in 1941 and which helped to exterminate almost the entire Jewish population.

The case was to have produced Britain's first war crimes trial under the controversial War Crimes Act, passed in 1991 under pressure from Jewish organisations. The government had to invoke rarely-used powers to force the act through parliament after it was rejected by the upper house.
